items.title: My self-hosted Docker apps update themselves, and automating everything was a piece of cake
items.summary: Docker was the first runtime I used when I dove into the self-hosting rabbit hole, and it has remained an essential aspect of my home lab ever since. After all, being able to self-host dozens of FOSS tools within isolated environments alone makes Docker a godsend when you want to break away from cloud-based, subscription-heavy apps. Combine that with its beginner-friendly ecosystem, portable images, and lightweight design, and you can see why I prefer Docker containers to dedicated virtual machines for my productivity services.

items.title: Running local LLMs in a Proxmox LXC is closer to bare metal than you’d think
items.summary: I'd always assumed a local LLM needed its own machine, or at least its own VM with the GPU passed straight through. I ignored that. My Strix Halo mini PC already runs Proxmox for my lab, so after switching my local AI setup to AMD's Lemonade, I dropped it into an LXC container and figured I'd move it to bare metal once it got too slow.

items.title: SolidPing: Self-Hosted Uptime Monitoring With Distributed Checks and Incident Management
items.summary: Keeping an eye on your homelab is relatively straightforward until you start juggling websites, databases, containers, and services spread across different networks. A simple HTTP check might tell you whether something responds, but it doesn't always explain why a service is failing or whether the problem is limited to a particular location. SolidPing takes a broader approach, combining uptime monitoring with distributed checks, incident management, and alerting in a self-hosted application. Monitoring From Multiple Locations SolidPing is an open-source monitoring platform built in Go that supports more than 40 check types.

items.title: Dockmesh is a Self-Hosted Docker Manager for Multiple Servers
items.summary: Managing Docker containers across several machines can get a little tedious. You might have a few applications running on a mini PC, another collection on a Proxmox VM, and a separate server handling everything else. Before long, you're switching between dashboards or connecting over SSH just to see what's running. Dockmesh is an open-source Docker management application that puts your servers under one web interface. It supports Docker Compose, application backups, and remote host management without requiring Kubernetes or Docker Swarm.

items.title: ARK: Survival Ascended: Community Crunch 533: A Matter of Scale
items.summary: When a dragon has two heads, run. When it’s the size of a Dodo and bristling with spikes... honestly, still run... unless it likes you. With its towering frame and twin jaws, Khoron is certainly hard to overlook. One head bears the jagged appearance of ancient stone, the other bristles with dark spines and a rather potent breath. But their differences run deeper than appearances, and Survivors unfortunate enough to cross their path may discover each head has its own way of dealing with unwelcome company.

items.title: Path of Exile streamer Zizaran's new Nordic ARPG blends PoE's depth with TFT's second-screen flexibility
items.summary: One of Path of Exile's most popular streamers has just unveiled an ARPG of his own, aiming to offer idle gameplay that's perfect for your second screen, but without losing the depth that makes RPGs like PoE 2 and Diablo 2 so beloved. Blastheim is that game, and it's being made by Twitch streamer 'Zizaran'

items.title: Tessera open-source dashboard for Home Assistant runs on ESP32 touchscreen devkits
items.summary: The open-source Tessera project enables neat dashboards for Home Assistant on affordable 2.8-inch to 10.1-inch ESP32 touchscreen (development) kits from CYD, Guition, and Waveshare. The Tessera firmware adds a layer to ESPHome firmware for display management, touchscreen handling, dashboard rendering, tiles, plugins, and more. It works in conjunction with the Tessera Screen Manager, which provides the Home Assistant interface to configure screens, manage layouts, install firmware, and push updates.

items.title: CachyOS Just Made One of Linux’s Biggest Gaming Problems Way Easier
items.summary: CachyOS is a distro pick that suits both power users and gamers alike. The installer offers 17+ desktop environments to pick from, and gamers get a Handheld Edition for devices like the Steam Deck and ROG Ally. Based on Arch Linux, it ships its own kernel and package builds for specific CPUs, while the installer comes as a GUI or a command-line version. CachyOS has now put out its sixth release of the year, and this one changes how the system boots, recovers, and installs software. The November Release CachyOS now has a dedicated kernel for games that use Epic's Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2.

items.title: XNU Linux Lets macOS Userspace Processes Run On Linux
items.summary: XNU Linux is a new opens-source project allowing macOS user-space software to run on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it. XNU Linux builds off Apple's open-source XNU kernel components of macOS while adapted to serve as a loadable Linux kernel module. Besides this XNU kernel module, this works on an otherwise unmodified ARM64 Linux system…

items.summary: Last week, Pax Dei gave some initial details about its upcoming Release 50, including major updates to plot permission features for clans and several revamps for jewelry and jewelcrafting. This week, Mainframe Industries has drilled down further, offering up some more granular details to address player questions and share some other features for the release as…

items.title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
items.summary: Buying a new computer in the last few years has meant wading through all manner of AI branding nonsense. Most of the AI pitches for laptops are little more than marketing hype, but the launch of Nvidia RTX Spark could bring a meaningful improvement in AI capabilities to the device you use every day. Asus has adopted Nvidia's new chip in its latest ProArt lineup, offering a staggering amount of memory to run local AI models. While it doesn't have a traditional GPU, the Asus ProArt P16, with up to 128GB of memory, can also be your primary gaming and productivity machine, but this unified experience comes at a high price.

items.title: Homelabber's $3,500 build straps four 32GB Nvidia V100s to a Lenovo mini PC for 128GB of VRAM
items.summary: A homelabber has built a local AI system out of four used 32GB Nvidia V100s and a refurbished Lenovo M720q Tiny mini PC. Ok_Kaleidoscope9103’s construction, detailed on Reddit, relies on the GPUs going over four OCuLink cables from a PCIe switch card, with a solder bridge on the riser and coreboot getting past a BIOS that only booted two cards. The quiet-running build has the full 128GB of VRAM and can hit about 285 tokens per second in total running Qwen3.8-27B across its four cards. The user, who gives his name as Michael, details his “home AI box” in a YouTube video billed as a “full build guide.”

items.summary: ear is fun. Who doesn’t love gear! But in the ultralight philosophy, you should actually strive to carry less of it. A minimalist backpacking setup won’t just save you money; it will keep your base weight low so you spend less time thinking about your aching knees and more time actually enjoying the trail. Remember: every ounce you don’t carry is an ounce you can brag about to all the other hikers around you. Today we’re taking ultralight to a whole new level with 6 surprising gear items you definitely will not need as a thru-hiker.

You'll explore the monastery and its grounds, solving puzzles and picking your way through interconnected areas as you find out what happened there.

items.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
items.summary: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon.

items.title: High Tide (Linux TIDAL client) adds support for DLNA, Chromecast
items.summary: High Tide, the open-source TIDAL client for Linux, can now play to Chromecast and DLNA devices like TVs and smart speakers. The feature rolls out in v1.8.0, released this weekend with a variety of smaller bug fixes and minor bumps, including showing artist names over Discord RPC. But it’s the wireless streaming that’s the big ticket. Most people use High Tide to stream music to the same device, and if wanting to punt audio elsewhere, could do it via Bluetooth. I’d also wager that most TIDAL subscribers own a device that can run the official apps.

items.title: Why Thanksgiving Football Emerged as an American Tradition in the Aftermath of the Civil War
items.summary: For many Americans, Thanksgiving is all about the three “f’s”: family, food and football. This year, that final “f” will be more present than ever, thanks to the addition of the National Football League’s first “ Thanksgiving Eve ” game on Wednesday, November 28. This faceoff, streaming on Netflix, joins the NFL’s three-game Thanksgiving Day lineup and its pick-me-up on Black Friday. It marks the latest in a series of expansions transforming the holiday slate from the dominion of the Detroit Lions—which played their first annual Thanksgiving game in 1934 and have only skipped the tradition six times since—to a three-day affair filled with more football than feasting.

items.title: Original Showa-Era ‘Ultraman’ Films Heading to Netflix For First Time
items.summary: Hot on the heels of Netflix scooping up Toho's Rebirth of Mothra trilogy over the summer, the streamer is going back to the vaults of Japanese monster cinema once again. Two classic Ultraman movies built from the original 1966 series are headed to Netflix globally, including in the United States, on December 2nd, 2026. The timing is fitting. 2026 marks 60 years since the Giant of Light first appeared on Japanese television, and while Netflix has been a home for modern takes on the character for…

items.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
items.summary: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years. Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible.

items.title: Sun news: On this date, 1st total solar eclipse seen from Antarctica
items.summary: Sun news November 23: On this date, the 1st total solar eclipse seen from Antarctica Today’s top story: On this date in 2003, a small group of lucky observers witnessed a rare total solar eclipse from Antarctica. Since 1900, only seven total eclipses have crossed the continent, and this was the first one anyone observed. The moon’s shadow swept over a remote stretch of the Southern Ocean and East Antarctica, taking an unusual path. Most eclipse shadows move east, but this one curved south and then west around the continent.

items.title: China details its path to a crewed Moon landing before 2030
items.summary: China has set out its most detailed roadmap yet for landing astronauts on the Moon before 2030, with three uncrewed missions planned before China’s first crew to leave Earth orbit will attempt the country’s first lunar landing. The lunar program builds on China’s continuing experience with the Tiangong space station, which prepares for its next crew rotation this month, including its first foreign visitor, one of two candidates from Pakistan. China first officially announced its crewed lunar landing plans at the Shenzhou-16 pre-launch press conference in Jiuquan on May 29, 2023.

items.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
items.summary: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices. In the future, this method could allow engineers to prototype faster, explore a wider range of chip designs, and discover new design schemes that might improve the performance and energy efficiency of robots, medical monitors, or industrial sensors.

items.title: Man critically hurt after rear-ending a semi-truck cab near Glendale-Phoenix border
items.summary: GLENDALE, AZ (AZFamily) — A man is in critical condition after his car slammed into the back of a semi-truck cab near the Glendale-Phoenix border early Sunday morning. Around 5 a.m., first responders were called to the crash in the area of 75th Avenue and Camelback Road, according to the Glendale Police Department. Officers found the man critically hurt, and paramedics took him to the hospital with life-threatening injuries. Investigators believe the man was speeding southbound in a Chevy Malibu when he rear-ended the cab of the semi.

items.title: AMD Preps More Graphics Driver Fixes For Linux 7.5, More DCN6 Enablement
items.summary: This week AMD sent out their latest batch of AMDGPU kernel graphics driver and AMDKFD kernel compute driver updates of work slated to land with the upcoming Linux 7.5 merge window. In addition to other code already submitted to DRM-Next for Linux 7.5 queuing, this week saw more AMDGPU/AMDKFD (and a few legacy Radeon) driver patches. This week the code churn was heavier on the fixes side. There was though more Display Core Next 6 "DCM6" IP work for that display block expected with next-gen RDNA 5 graphics processors.

items.title: Stalwart 1.2 Offers Open-Source Microsoft Exchange Replacement
items.summary: Stalwart, the open-source mail and collaboration server written in Rust, has released version 1.2, introducing compatibility with Microsoft Exchange protocols. The update lets organizations replace their Exchange infrastructure with a self-hosted solution while continuing to use familiar email clients, including Microsoft Outlook. The main addition is support for MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services, Exchange ActiveSync, and Autodiscover. These protocols allow Exchange-compatible clients to connect to Stalwart and access email, calendars, contacts, tasks, and notes through a single account.

items.title: ‘Destination landmark’ with resort and golf course eyed for Gilbert park
items.summary: A five-star resort and 18-hole golf course could reshape a 272-acre master-planned park in south Gilbert. The catch: Millions in taxpayer dollars are already earmarked for a different project underway at the same site. Gilbert Regional Park has been in motion since 2015, when the town entered into a 225-acre easement agreement with the Flood Control District of Maricopa County to turn a flood-control basin into a recreational park with sports fields, playgrounds, basketball courts and other amenities.

items.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
items.summary: On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft.

items.title: A LEASH for AI-controlled robots: New system could reduce harmful actions
items.summary: Large language models, the models behind the functioning of ChatGPT, Gemini and similar platforms, are now also used in robotics. These models can help robots to interpret user instructions, plan their actions and respond to changes in their surroundings.

items.title: Your Linux Laptop Won't Suspend? Here's What You Can Do
items.summary: You close the lid and the laptop keeps running. Or you leave it alone for an hour and it never goes to sleep. Often nothing is broken. The cause is a program that asked systemd to hold off sleep. That request is called an inhibitor lock. In this article, you'll list the locks on your system, read what each one blocks, tell a lock that stops a suspend from one that only delays it, and close the program that holds it. Every command here works on any distribution that uses systemd. I ran them on an Ubuntu 26.04 desktop virtual machine with GNOME, which ships systemd 259.

items.title: Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites postponed due to a technical issue
items.summary: Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft has been postponed due to a technical issue. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation was scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Monday (Nov. 23). However, the countdown was halted following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace. The countdown was stopped before the removal of the mobile gantry, with Arianespace confirming that the rocket and its satellite payload remain safe and stable.

items.title: Linux 7.5 To Introduce Initial Mainline Support For Ambarella SoCs
items.summary: Following some initial Device Tree and driver preparation patches that were merged for Linux v7.4, the upcoming Linux v7.5 kernel is set to introduce initial support for Ambarella SoCs with the CV75 being the initial SoC target. Ambarella has been around since 2004 as a California company focused on SoCs for computer vision and AI edge applications. Finally with Linux 7.5 in 2027 is set to be mainline kernel support for the first with their CV75 being the first SoC target from them. This merge made it into the soc/soc.git's "for-next" Git branch this past week introducing the "ARCH_AMBARELLA" Kconfig and the various Device Tree additions.

items.title: HTA Design unveils "UK's largest council housing development"
items.summary: A collection of brick-clad buildings containing over 450 homes forms Kidbrooke Park Road in London, which architecture studio HTA Design claims is the largest new-build council housing development in the UK. Built on a formerly disused site in Greenwich, the development contains 452 homes, all of which are social housing. Construction company Durkan delivered Kidbrooke Park Road for the Royal Borough of Greenwich as part of its council housing programme, Greenwich Builds. HTA Design said the project "demonstrates what can be achieved when local authorities take an ambitious approach to housing delivery".

items.title: Meet AMAA, Neri&Hu’s pick for the most influential architect of the next 20 years
items.summary: An innovative approach to the reuse of existing buildings defines the output of Italian architecture office AMAA, which Neri&Hu has selected as one of 20 names to watch in architecture and design as part of Dezeen's 20×20 project, sponsored by Kohler. Led by Marcello Galiotto and Alessandra Rampazzo, over the past 14 years AMAA has become known for its approach to the reuse of post-industrial structures in northern Italy, with the transformation of a former factory building into its own studio, a typical example of its approach.

items.title: RIBA president rejoins ARB register to restore architect title
items.summary: The president of the Royal Institute of British Architects, Chris Williamson, has decided to renew his membership with the Architects Registration Board, nearly a year after terminating it. In a LinkedIn post, Williamson said he was rejoining the Architects Registration Board's (ARB) register because he no longer wanted "to face the prospect of legal action". Specifically, he said he feared the potential "legal proceedings and financial penalties" from referring to himself as an architect, which ARB does not permit if a person is unregistered.

items.title: KaOS 2026.11 Drops KDE Plasma and Qt 5, Moves Forward with Niri
items.summary: KaOS, the independent rolling-release Linux distro, has announced version 2026.11, its latest stable installation ISO, with KDE Plasma and Qt 5 now completely removed from the distro’s repositories. The removal of Plasma follows the project’s decision to move away from systemd and adopt a Wayland-based desktop built around the Niri compositor and Noctalia shell. Developers say Plasma no longer fits the distribution’s new direction, especially its effort to reduce systemd dependencies. KaOS 2026.11 ships with Niri 26.04 and Noctalia 5.6.

items.title: Old-school Linux desktops find fresh routes to Wayland
items.summary: Xfce's next release is taking shape for 2027, while MATE users have fresh options for moving their familiar desktop onto Wayland. One of the oldest surviving Linux desktops has a relatively slow release schedule: new stable releases of Xfce tend to appear every two years. The project just updated its release engineering roadmap for the forthcoming Xfce 4.22, and it looks like the next version won't arrive until early next year. We covered the release of Xfce 4.20 in December 2024, but 4.22 is still incubating.

items.title: SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video)
items.summary: SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. items.title: Linux 7.4-rc4 Released: "It's Huge. What A Surprise."
items.summary: Linux 7.4-rc4 is out today as the newest weekly test candidate for Linux 7.4. Continuing to be fueled by AI/LLM generated bug reports and patches, the Linux 7.4 cycle remains quite active. Linux 7.4-rc4 was another busy week and now mid-way through the release candidate process in working toward the stable Linux 7.4 kernel by late December. Some of the notable changes that crossed my radar this week were removing NVMe namespaces in parallel for better performance and the CPU family/model IDs being added for Intel Razor Lake and Coral Rapids processors.

items.title: "Sacred" archaeological finds become raw materials for design in Ex Situ exhibition
items.summary: New objects made from mammoth bone, leather from the middle ages and stumps from a road built under Roman Emperor Hadrian feature in the Ex Situ project, set to be exhibited soon in The Hague. Initiated and curated by Dutch designer Marisa Klaster, working in concert with archaeologist René Isarin, the project makes use of materials that many in Isarin's profession and the broader public might consider off-limits for new designs: the finds from archaeological digs. However, while these finds, such as 40,000-year-old mammoth bone and 14th-century ship wood, sound like they belong in a museum, they are in fact deselected – not chosen for inclusion in any archives.

items.title: Reduce, resharpen, reuse: Ancient stone tools reveal a regional pattern in southwest China
items.summary: The value of a stone tool can long outlast its first sharp edge. Across 27 locations in southwest China, archaeologists have found evidence of a toolmaking approach that preserved enough stone to allow repeated sharpening—and sometimes the same piece was used as both a tool and a source of fresh flakes for new cutting edges.

items.title: After 20 years of helping kids read, an Arizona school volunteer gets a surprise birthday from students
items.summary: Larry Dodson thought he was coming to school Friday for a pancake breakfast. Instead, he walked out to a courtyard full of students singing Happy Birthday. Staff at Sierra Verde STEAM Academy organized the surprise to thank Dodson, a volunteer who has worked at the school for 20 years and turns 85 next week. Students wore bracelets that read I want to be like Larry, and Dodson was given a shirt that said Im Larry. It was very heartwarming, Dodson said. You dont have a surprise birthday party with 900 guests singing happy birthday to you.

items.title: Opel and Leapmotor formalise battery-electric SUV partnership
items.summary: Opel and Leapmotor have officially agreed to collaborate on the development of a new electric SUV. With a launch date penned for 2028, the model will use key components from the Chinese manufacturer and will be produced at Stellantis' plant in Zaragoza, Spain.

items.summary: Serafini Productions was busy during The Horror Game Awards, releasing a sextet of trailers and giving fans an update on previously-announced titles in the BrokenLore series, as well as the the announcement of a new third-person survival horror title, Ugly Within. Making its world premiere at the show, Ugly Within centers around the home of the Kamata family, a traditional estate hiding a history it was never meant to share and an entity the family has worshipped for generations.

items.title: Presidential villa suffers water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says
items.summary: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu says the presidential villa suffers from cuts in electricity and water - issues that are all too common for the country's ordinary citizens. He said he was shaving last week when the water supply cut at the villa, known as Aso Rock, in Abuja. He is seeking re-election next January and vowed to address these issues. Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos. items.title: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy
items.summary: Autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year. A sharp spike in mortgage rates in September has pushed the already chilly real estate sector into a deep freeze. Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business. The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily. By the start of October, it was at 7.61%, a full percentage point higher. items.title: Q&A: Enabling more human-like interactions and understanding in multimodal foundation models
items.summary: Humans experience and interact with the world through sensory information. This could mean learning correspondences between the sound of bird chirps and the word “robin,” or being able to visually identify and follow your friend “Sarah” in a crowd of people. In many cases, people are able to draw on their latent “multimodal” knowledge — information across multiple data types, from audio to video to text or spoken word — to perform these tasks without many, or sometimes even any, examples. items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
items.summary: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time. Now, researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models that can ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds, based on what is actually possible in the real world.

items.title: A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
items.summary: On a superconducting processor, we turned one of quantum mechanics’ strangest features into something you can measure, benchmark, and put to work across systems as large as 105 qubits. Here is a Sunday paper-style puzzle you can try right now. Draw a 3×3 grid. Fill every cell with either +1 or −1, subject to two rules: each row must multiply to +1, and each column must multiply to −1. You didn’t manage it, right? There is an elegant reason for that. For a row to multiply to +1, it needs an even number of −1s.

items.summary: From cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to lithium deposits in Mali and uranium reserves in Niger, Africa’s mineral wealth is becoming an increasingly important arena of competition between the United States, China and Russia. items.summary: There’s a tendency within modern audiences to think about horror as always having elements of the supernatural, yet that isn’t always the case. items.title: Pangolin 1.27 Tunneled Reverse Proxy Adds Centralized Client Management
items.summary: Pangolin, the open-source remote access platform that combines a zero-trust VPN and reverse proxy, has just released v1.27. The main addition is managed client settings, allowing administrators to enforce connection configurations based on user roles from the Pangolin dashboard. With the new functionality, administrators can centrally control DNS settings, upstream DNS servers, exit node selection, MTU values, and local route preferences. These policies apply automatically when a client connects, and users cannot modify settings enforced by administrators.

Over the next few days, the company, Zimmer Biomet, texted four times. Russak didn’t understand the inquiries asking him to use an app, he said. items.summary: Over 2,500 years ago, Himera was a Greek colony inhabited by local Sicilians, Phoenicians and Greeks. Despite their diverse cultural backgrounds, they all shared one thing: they began weaning their babies early and continued for a long time.

items.title: Soddy’s Hexlet
items.summary: Set two spheres against one another and wrap them in a third, as shown. Now add a new sphere, tangent to the first two and to the large enclosing sphere. Surprisingly, if you keep adding these new spheres, tangent to one another, they’ll always form a “necklace” of six. English radiochemist Frederick Soddy discovered this pretty fact in 1937, though it had been known to Japanese mathematicians since at least 1822. Soddy, who had written a paean to Descartes’ theorem in Nature in June 1936, added another that December to celebrate his finding: However ill-assorted in girth three spheres may be Each one can kiss the other two simultaneously A ring of six about them all kissing serially.

items.title: Possible Ancient Tavern Investigated Near Baghdad
items.summary: BAGHDAD, IRAQ— La Brújula Verde reports that researchers led by Nicola Laneri of the University of Catania are continuing to excavate the site of a 3,800-year-old building at Tell Muhammad, which is located near the Tigris River in central Iraq. A cuneiform tablet recording an agreement to borrow barley and beer was found in one of the building’s rooms. The contract had been signed in front of two witnesses. The space where the tablet was uncovered features a semicircular mudbrick counter facing the street, and a mudbrick basin that may have been used for brewing or making bread.

items.title: Students Recover Roman Military Artifacts in Northern England
items.summary: REDESDALE, ENGLAND—A student excavation at a site on the Roman frontier in northeastern England uncovered several artifacts linked to Roman elites and military service, according to a statement released by Newcastle University. The first, a piece of gold chain measuring almost three inches long, is made of individual rings that were pinched into figure-eight shapes, folded, and then interwoven. A small lead sheet bearing a Latin inscription may have been used as a personal message, a curse tablet, or a commercial seal.

items.title: Git-Bug 0.12 Overhauls Caching, Adds Native Git Transport
items.summary: Git-bug, the distributed Git-based issue tracker that lets developers manage bugs and issues directly within their repositories without relying on a centralized service, has released version 0.12. items.title: White Sands National Park: Things to Do & Where to Camp Nearby
items.summary: Picture this: you wax up a plastic saucer, push off the top of a sugar-white dune, and look up mid-run to see the jagged San Andres Mountains stretched across the horizon. Then you hike back up and do it again. And again, until the sun slips behind those peaks and the whole dunefield glows pink and gold. That’s what happens White Sands National Park, which protects much of the world’s largest gypsum dunefield: 275 square miles of glittering sand in southern New Mexico’s Tularosa Basin. The sand stays cool under bare feet even on warm days, the Sacramento Mountains light up at sunset, and once it’s dark, the stars put on a show of their own.

items.summary: Space exploration tends to suck up most of the oxygen when it comes to venturing out into the unknown. But there’s an arguably even more mysterious frontier hidden beneath us. Nowhere is that more real than at Challenger Deep. The deepest known point on Earth, Challenger Deep is located in the 1,580-mile-long Mariana Trench at the floor of the Pacific Ocean. Getting to the bottom of this ancient chasm means diving more than 6.8 miles (around 36,000 feet) underwater. For a sense of scale, Mount Everest could be dropped into this chasm, and its summit still wouldn’t reach the surface.

items.title: Motion under the ocean explains the depth of the world’s deepest spot
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) Challenger Deep is the deepest valley in the deepest trench in the ocean, plunging to roughly 11,000 meters below sea level. Now, scientists have a new clue about how it got to be so … well, deep. Challenger Deep is found within the Mariana Trench, a crescent-shaped gouge in the seafloor east of the Philippines in the Pacific Ocean. The trench is the scene of a slo-mo tectonic collision called a subduction zone: The Pacific plate is diving beneath the Mariana plate, bending downward as it sinks into the mantle, forming a steep trench on the ocean floor.

items.title: 9 Facts About Georg Baselitz, the Painter Who Turned Art Upside Down
items.summary: Georg Baselitz, who died in April 2026 at the age of 88, was one of the most influential German painters of the postwar era. Raised in what became East Germany, he moved to the West after being expelled from an East Berlin art school that drilled its students in Socialist Realism. As a Neo-Expressionist and a painter of human figures, Baselitz shook up modern art in 1969 by painting his subjects upside down, forcing viewers to look at the painting itself rather than what it depicted. items.title: Why Norman Rockwell’s Perfect Thanksgiving Painting Angered Europe
items.summary: American painter and illustrator Norman Rockwell is best known for portraying an idealized image of American life during the 20th century, one that has attracted equal amounts of criticism and praise. Nowhere is this more evident than in his depiction of the Thanksgiving dinner, in the now iconic Freedom from Want, which presented a white, middle-class family gathered around a glistening turkey, basking in the warm glow of shared wealth and emotional connection. As much as the painting’s indulgent tone angered Europeans struggling with wartime austerity and sparked racial controversy, it also became the quintessential ideal that so many Thanksgiving dinners aspired to be.

The company, which serves about 2.4 million customers across south-east England, recorded a pre-tax loss of Â£22.9m in the six months to 30 September, compared with a profit of Â£18.2m during the same period last year. In July, regulator Ofwat ordered the company to spend Â£30.5m on improvements after supply interruptions hit customers across Kent and Sussex which affected more than 286,000 customers.

items.title: Qatar Airways Adds 1st Ever Airbus A321LR Routes: See Map Now
items.summary: Qatar Airways has not received its first Airbus A321LR yet. The latest information is that it'll be delivered at the end of 2026, which is just a few weeks away. Given this, the one world member has disclosed its first two routes on the new variant. Each week, airlines from around the world submit schedule changes to OAG and Cirium Diio. In the latest update, Qatar Airways disclosed that its first two A321LR routes are due to be from Doha to both Vienna and Zurich, but things could change. While subject to the exact date on which the initial airframe arrives in Doha and entry into service procedures, the first passenger-carrying A321LR service is due to take place on January 4, 2027.

items.title: The Boeing 737 NG Fuel Saver That Was First Introduced As A Retrofit, But Became A Factory Option On Later Builds
items.summary: The tall blended winglets on the 737 Next Generation became one of the narrowbody’s most recognizable features, but the design did not originate at Boeing. Aviation Partners developed it for business jets, and the two companies formed a joint venture to bring it to Boeing aircraft. Boeing then announced it as a factory option for the 737-800 in early 2000.

items.title: The Unexpected Reason Airlines Still Fly the Boeing 767
items.summary: In this video, we'll explore why airlines like Delta and Icelandair are deploying Boeing 767s on relatively short routes, how premium cabins and passenger demand make these flights profitable, and why the aircraft's final years could look very different from the missions that made it famous.

items.title: LATAM Airlines unveils cabin interiors for its upcoming A321XLR fleet
items.summary: LATAM Airlines has officially unveiled the cabin design for its upcoming Airbus A321XLR fleet. While some elements of the new cabins had already been disclosed in April 2026, on November 18, 2026, the airline’s CEO, Roberto Alvo, shared a video on LinkedIn, which depicted what the cabin of the new aircraft will look like. The aircraft will be configured to carry 174 passengers and will include 12 Premium Business suites and 162 seats in Economy, 36 of which will be more spacious.

items.title: One Small Step
items.summary: How did Friday manage to leave a single footprint for Robinson Crusoe to discover? I went up the shore, and down the shore, but it was all one; I could see no other impression but that one. I went to it again to see if there were any more, and to observe if it might not be my fancy; but there was no room for that, for there was exactly the very print of a foot — toes, heel, and every part of a foot. How it came thither I knew not, nor could in the least imagine. “Was the single footprint made by some monstrous hopping cannibal?” asks John Sutherland in The Folio Book of Literary Puzzles (2007).

items.title: Ubuntu 27.04 daily builds are available to download
items.summary: If you plan to track development of Ubuntu 27.04 ‘Tenacious T-Rex’ up close, daily build images are now available for download. Daily builds are produced for the duration of a development cycle, right up until the final, stable release. They’re built from development code (obviously) and produced (almost) daily, to make testing changes easier. Those who don’t have specific need to test shouldn’t, but those who need or want to don’t need to wait for the public beta, or go to the hassle of upgrading from an earlier release (that’s possible too, btw).

items.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets through its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
items.summary: Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos. By Sergio De Simone…

items.title: The Foolproof Southern Pecan Pie I Make Every Year (People Beg for the Recipe)
items.summary: Thanksgiving simply isn’t complete without pie. While pumpkin and apple tend to get all the glory, let’s not overlook a Southern favorite: pecan pie. Thanks to our Food Editor Patty Catalano, even a novice baker can master this quintessential Thanksgiving dessert. Here’s how. Get the recipe: Pecan Pie If you’re on pie duty this year, don’t worry: This pecan pie recipe is super-easy to make.

items.title: 3 ’80s Sci-Fi Movies I Want to Watch for the First Time Again Because They Still Blow My Mind
items.summary: Thanks to rapid technological acceleration, the ’80s was a fantastic decade for science fiction. The development of personal computing and major leaps in filmmaking techniques created the perfect storm for filmmakers imagining other worlds or looking into the future. The ’80s boom expanded beyond the simple space settings that directors in the 1970s started with and branched out into a wide range of subgenres. There are far too many stellar ’80s sci-fi films to mention in this article, including Blade Runner, The Terminator, RoboCop, Brazil, The Fly, E.T., Akira, Back to the Future, and many, many more.

items.title: Julia Child's "Legendary" Potato Side Dish Lives Up To The Hype
items.summary: It's so creamy. The Kitchn: Julia Child's "Legendary" Potato Side Dish Lives Up To The Hype.

items.title: 37 Thanksgiving Cocktails and Drinks for Every Guest
items.summary: Big-batch punches, low-alcohol spritzes, NA drinks for keeping it cute, and nightcaps for when all is said and done. Whether you’re pouring a cup of cheer or drinking to steel your nerves against Great-Aunt Edna, these Thanksgiving cocktails cover every angle. There are the cranberry, apple, and maple flavors we crave this time of year, plus big-batch drinks that won’t keep you playing bartender all afternoon. We’re talking freezer-ready martinis, bourbon punch, and a cranberry mule that guests can spike themselves.

items.title: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports
items.summary: Brussels Airport (BRU) expects major flight disruption on November 23, after some air traffic controllers at Belgian air navigation service provider skeyes announced they would join a national demonstration. The airport said most arriving and departing flights will have to be cancelled because skeyes will not be able to provide normal air traffic control services during the action. The disruption is expected from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time (6 a.m. – 8 p.m. UTC). Skeyes unable to provide normal ATC services According to Skeyes, the expected number of staff would not be enough to safely handle regular air traffic during the strike.

items.title: Christmas Travel Chaos Looms as Lufthansa Pilots Give Airline Final Deadline
items.summary: FRANKFURT – Lufthansa (LH) faces renewed strike pressure after German pilots’ union Vereinigung Cockpit (VC) gave the airline until November 23, 2026, to reconsider its position in a long-running dispute over pensions, pay and job security. The deadline comes after seven months of negotiations and 18 rounds of mediation failed to produce an agreement. No strike has been announced, but the union has warned that further industrial action remains possible if Lufthansa fails to move toward the mediator’s proposed settlement.

items.title: Jared Padalecki's Supernatural Revival Idea Is Good, But There's Already A Better Option
items.summary: Supernatural has been off the air since 2020, but the idea of a reboot has long been on the mind of the show's beloved fanbase, and there's already an angle that works even better to bring Sam (Jared Padalecki) and Dean Winchester (Jensen Ackles) than Padalecki's recent idea. Despite Supernatural spanning the course of 15 seasons and over 300 episodes, the series has long been one that its fanbase is looking for more of. Whether that's been through comic book continuations or series spinoffs over the past few years, the show is beloved enough that viewers are always ready for more.

items.title: A fungus that can survive in Chernobyl could help create materials that trap and break down nerve agents and pesticides
items.summary: Deep inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone, where radiation levels have remained unsafe for people for the past 40 years, black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine. They’re entirely undeterred by the radiation – in fact, some fungi even grow toward it. The same type of species, Cladosporium sphaerospermum, has grown on the International Space Station, about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above the surface of the Earth, in an experiment to test its resistance to radiation.

items.title: Silver briefly forms a rare crystal structure seen in radioactive polonium
items.summary: How atoms are arranged in a material shapes many of its properties. The same carbon atoms, for example, can form diamond and graphite depending on how they are arranged, giving rise to materials with vastly different chemical and physical properties. Now, researchers at Hokkaido University have discovered a new crystal structure of silver with unusually high chemical reactivity. The findings, published in Nano Letters, could open new avenues for exploring materials with desirable properties.

items.title: Not Olive Oil: Marinate Seafood In This Store-Bought Italian Staple For 10x More Flavor
items.summary: The often mild taste of seafood can benefit from olive oil's fruity notes, but sometimes, we want a different flavor direction. That's why we like marinating our seafood in pesto, which adds a sunny herbaceous quality to the final dish. We asked New York Times food journalist Melissa Clark, who recently published a new cookbook, " The Big Book of Dinner: Recipes and Rules (and How to Break Them)," for some tips, tricks, and general rules on how to marinate seafood in pesto. Clark says, "Cover the seafood with the pesto up to 12 hours ahead and refrigerate before cooking.

items.title: Dutch F-35As and French Rafales operate from Finnish highway strip
items.summary: Dutch F-35As and French Rafales have operated from the Jännevirta highway strip in eastern Finland during Protective Fence 26, the Finnish Air Force’s main exercise of the year, as NATO allies practice dispersing their fighters away from conventional air bases. The Dutch Ministry of Defense said on November 20, 2026, that several F-35As had landed on Highway 9 near Kuopio that day. The Finnish Air Force reported that French Rafales deployed to Rovaniemi had carried out touch-and-go landings at the same location, marking the first time the French fighter had operated from a Finnish highway.

items.title: Docker Compose is better than clicking through a GUI, and how to start in 10 minutes
items.summary: Spinning up a container usually starts with a dashboard, since it's already open and the buttons are right there. It's convenient because you can set every port, volume, and variable on the fly, but the reasoning behind each choice stays in your head. If you open the same setup months later, you might not remember why any of it works.

items.title: Inside Joramco’s expansion: New hangars, smarter maintenance and global ambitions
items.summary: Joramco is preparing for its next phase of expansion, building on the success of Hangar 7 with two additional hangars planned in Jordan, a growing pipeline of aircraft maintenance engineers and new digital technologies designed to make its operations more efficient. Speaking to AeroTime at MRO Europe in Amsterdam, held from October 27 to 29, 2026, Fraser Currie, Chief Strategy and Commercial Officer at DAE Engineering, outlined how the company intends to build on its growing international presence while keeping workforce development and safety at the heart of its strategy.

items.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
items.summary: In a normal session, Claude asks for one tool call, reads the full result, and decides the next step. In Code Mode, one script can run commands in parallel, pass one result into the next call, and return only the output the model needs. The documentation's example finds a file with rg, raises a retry limit, runs the tests, and returns just the path and test output. The conversation still shows each tool call and diff, while the generated code sits in the transcript viewer. Anthropic recommends it for edits repeated across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands.

items.title: A New Jean-Michel Basquiat Documentary Considers the Artist Behind the Work
items.summary: A forthcoming documentary spotlights the life and work of luminary artist Jean-Michel Basquiat (1960-1988). Directed by Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman for Netflix, the feature film is the first project authorized by the artist’s two younger sisters, Lisane Basquiat and Jeanine Heriveaux, who helm his estate. In a trailer, the siblings describe their brother’s energetic approach to life and how the story typically told about his meteoric rise omits so much of who he really was. Simply titled Jean-Michel Basquiat, the film features archival footage and audio, along with never-before-seen works and commentary from his family.

items.title: DOJ honors Goodyear police officer who rescued woman from burning car on I-10
items.summary: Officer Dakota Berry of Goodyear was recognized by the U.S. Department of Justice for his distinguished service.

items.title: Shōzen TV Anime Unveils New Trailer, Key Visual, Cast
items.summary: The staff for Shōzen, the television anime adaptation of Jiang Jia Meizi 's Chinese manhua Shang Shan, revealed a new trailer, key visual, and another cast member on Sunday. Kana Hanazawa plays Ko Kuka, Dōzen's childhood friend who shares a special bond with him. The series will debut on the B8station programming block on Fuji TV and other venues in April 2027. The story follows a Taoist priest Dōzen who encounters a young girl raised by supernatural creatures during his travels. He names the girl Shōzen, adopting her as his disciple, as he teaches her about human emotion and love.

items.title: 9 Classic Fantasy Books Perfect To
items.summary: There are certain books that stay with you throughout your life. Others, you come back to, perhaps unexpectedly, and they provide a new meaning. This is especially true of genres like fantasy, which tend to attract readers of all ages, with very different understandings of the world. As a child or teenager, one may be enthralled by a book’s plot, reading as fast as possible. For an older reader, or a person who has read the book before, the story serves another purpose. The act of reading becomes about the joys of the journey: breaking down the worldbuilding, looking for clues for a plot twist, or understanding lessons that went over one’s head the first time around.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.summary: I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry.

items.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
items.summary: Growing up in the French Alps, Julie Daoust fell for mushrooms early in life. "So as a kid, we'd go out and forage," she recalls. "We'd come across species like lion's mane or reishi. And I became more and more interested in those species." Daoust went on to get a Ph.D. in chemistry, searching nature for novel pharmaceuticals. Her work ultimately led her back to mushrooms, a group of organisms to which humans are more closely related than plants. And yet, many of our modern medicines and therapeutics come from plants.

items.title: Forgotten Lampshades Become Playful Chandeliers in This Romanian Designer’s Lighting Collection
items.summary: There is something undeniably charming about objects that carry traces of the past. Their imperfections, unusual proportions, and familiar textures often hold a character that contemporary manufacturing struggles to recreate. With Lampa Volta, Romanian designer Mihai Popescu embraces this character, transforming forgotten lampshades into a lighting collection that feels earthy, expressive, and quietly luxurious. What began as a fascination with discarded objects has evolved into a celebration of craftsmanship, materiality, and the beauty of giving old things new purpose.

items.title: ‘We’re Still Here’ Celebrates Remarkable Quilts by 15 Contemporary Black Artists
items.summary: In the wee hours of a busy Saturday morning, on June 28, 1969, police raided The Stonewall Inn in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village, a renowned hangout for the LGBTQ+ community. During the 1950s and 1960s, few businesses openly welcomed gay people, and the legal system was against them—even two consenting adults in the privacy of their own home could face years in prison or a psychiatric institution if convicted of the crime of sodomy. Bar raids were common, but this one was particularly fraught due to the volume of people, and police quickly lost control.

items.title: Elegance Flows Through Sheena Liam’s Embroideries in Green
items.summary: Model and ballet dancer Sheena Liam brings her understanding of poise, elegance, and graceful bodily movements to a more fixed medium. For the past several years, the artist has been stitching tender portraits of women with long, three-dimensional braids that cascade off the fabric. Occasionally, a single loose thread appears to have slipped out of its plait as it drifts across a protagonist’s cheek. Liam’s latest works are on view this month in her solo exhibition, The Unbearable Lightness. Several pieces feature figures sporting the same striped bodysuit with an open back, and the methodical pattern on the garment evokes both a sense of precision and rhythm depicted in the scenes.

items.title: Hugh Jackman Has Always Wanted To Play One Iconic Horror Movie Villain
items.summary: Fans of 1980s slasher movies would do well to track down Daniel Farrands' 2013 documentary "Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th," a wildly thorough, 400-minute film that unpacks every single movie in the long-running "Friday the 13th" franchise. Indeed, the documentary even briefly reveals that Hugh Jackman once dreamed of playing Jason Voorhees (!) in the property. Jackman's first screen credit came in 1994, when he appeared on the Australian drama series "Law of the Land," and he made his feature film debut five years later.

items.title: Sticky Miso Chicken and More Recipes We Made This Week
items.summary: It’s no secret that Bon Appétit editors cook a lot for work. So it should come as no surprise that we cook a lot during our off hours too. Here are the recipes we’re whipping up this month to get dinner on the table, entertain our friends, satisfy a sweet tooth, use up leftovers, and everything in between. For even more staff favorites, click here. November 20 Apple picking → snacking cake My husband and I recently took our 3-year-old daughter apple picking. As expected at the tail end of the season, the only apples left were Granny Smith.

items.title: Commentary: Helping the Colorado River, one rock at a time
items.summary: When I was 12 years old, a flood took about 40 acres of my uncle’s property along the Virgin River in northwestern Arizona. I remember that event. I’ve lived here my whole life, and when you live and work along a river, you realize it’s not a question of if the river will change, but when. Over the years, I’ve used rock to support the banks and retain the agricultural land behind them. When the Arizona Game and Fish Department approached me about a different way to place rock in the river, I was interested.

items.title: Mission: Yozakura Family Season 2 Anime's 2nd Part Casts Shinichirō Miki
items.summary: The staff for the anime of Hitsuji Gondaira 's Mission: Yozakura Family ( Yozakura-san Chi no Daisakusen ) manga announced on Sunday Shinichirō Miki will join the cast of the second part of the second season in episode 47, which airs on November 29. Miki plays Asa, a man who holds the key to solving the mysteries of the story. The second part of the second season premiered on MBS, TBS, and 26 other channels on October 11 at 5:00 p.m. (4:00 a.m. EDT). High school student Taiyou Asano has been socially inept ever since his family died in a car crash.

items.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
items.summary: Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools. They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats. More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning. Police in Erfurt in Thuringia were among the first to issue a statement on the threats, saying they were responding to threats at "multiple schools" after morning warnings, including in Jena, Erfurt, Mühlhausen, Zella-Mehlis, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt and Greiz.

items.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
items.summary: When does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz? When you're in a German cinema. For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar -winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich. The same goes for all other famous actors. In Germany's €125-million ($138-million) voiceover industry, Hollywood 's up-and-comers are "adopted" by a voice actor who provides their German voice — often for decades — ensuring continuity and a certain relationship to the stars for audiences.

items.title: Stephen King's Forgotten 2000s Horror Anthology Series Adapted 8 Of His Short Stories
items.summary: Stephen King is almost as prolific on the small screen as he is on bookstore shelves. Today, we have the surprisingly scary and gruesome "It: Welcome to Derry," but this is just the latest in a long line of shows that have either directly adapted the author's stories or used them as inspiration. With so many King series scattered throughout TV history, it's inevitable that many have gone overlooked and under-appreciated. "Nightmares & Dreamscapes" is a prime example of an underrated Stephen King show.

items.title: Space colony sim Oxygen Not Included brings DLC features to the base game in a big new quality-of-life update
items.summary: Developer Klei Interactive has just released a new Oxygen Not Included update that brings a wealth of welcome improvements to its interstellar colony sim. The Don't Starve studio's side-scrolling, base-building management game is one of the best in its genre, with a 95% user review average putting it in close contention with the likes of…

items.title: ‘Tales from the Darkside’ and ‘Amazing Stories’ Thanksgiving Horror TV Episodes Prove the Holiday Deserves More Terror
items.summary: The reasons why horror generally overlooks Thanksgiving would require a longer discussion, but the fact of the matter is that the day in November for feasts and togetherness has simply never been a popular backdrop in the genre. As scarcely seen as the holiday is in horror movies, it may be even more so in horror television. With that said, we have at least two classic anthology series that don’t omit Thanksgiving from their fantastical offerings. These certain episodes of Tales from the Darkside and Amazing Stories make a case for Thanksgiving being a missed opportunity for holiday terror.

items.title: This Creamy Side Dish That Dominated The '70s Is The Green Bean Casserole Swap You Need
items.summary: Food trends come and go. On one end, you have TikTok trends and viral recipe hacks. On the other, you have the baked, boiled, and often overcooked dishes that are all too familiar to boomers. Casseroles tend to fall on the latter end. A few casseroles have weathered the trends, like green bean casserole, which is now a Thanksgiving standby. It's worth revisiting recipes that have fallen out of favor, though. Your family may never forgive you if you serve unusual vintage casserole dishes (like the 1920s recipe featuring lima beans and marshmallows), but they'll likely welcome a creamy, '70s-style broccoli and cheddar bake.

items.title: Sabrent Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger Quick Look
items.summary: Sabrent sent us this charger, and while we do not generally review USB chargers, we thought we would take a few photos and share it since it has been pretty useful. The Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger is a desktop charging station with four USB-C ports and four USB-A ports, and Sabrent rates it at 252W of total output. That is a lot of power for something that sits on a desk, and the port layout is what makes it worth a closer look. The enclosure is a black rectangular block that is not really what we would want from a travel charger, but it works well on a desk.

items.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
items.summary: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices.

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Easter Eggs Found Involving Satanic Rituals, Aliens, ‘Manhunt’, and ‘Silent Hill’!
items.summary: You had to know that Rockstar had more than just a “Dexter” reference in store for players in Grand Theft Auto VI. It turns out that Rockstar has added in Easter Eggs where you can encounter ghosts, Satanic rituals, aliens, and even a random encounter that makes reference to their classic stealth horror title Manhunt mashed up with Saw! These Easter Eggs are done solo, as they won’t trigger if you are with your partner. YouTuber Punish has documented these newly-discovered Easter Eggs on their channel, kicking off with a chance encounter with a ghostly woman figure that appeared under a streetlight while they were driving around at night (naturally).

items.summary: The staff for the second television anime season based on nigozyu and Umibōzu 's The Detective Is Already Dead ( Tantei wa Mō, Shindeiru. ) light novel series revealed a new visual and promotional video on Sunday for the show's new arc. Kadokawa previously announced that the second season would air in July, but then delayed it to October. Crunchyroll is streaming the series as it airs and is also streaming an English dub. New cast members include Akari Komiyama as Mia Whitlock and Nobuhiko Okamoto as Scarlet.

items.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
items.summary: From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex, a new book of short stories written by kids who are part of the "Read Alex" literacy program in Johannesburg. Participants in weekly classes wrote stories drawing on their own lives.'/> South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors.

items.title: A Treetop View Without the Fishbowl: John Lautner’s Baldwin House
items.summary: From Micheltorena Street, the Baldwin Residence looks like a low roof behind a hedge, with a ribbon of windows tucked under the eaves. From downhill, the same house seems to hang in the treetops. The difference gets at the problem John Lautner had to solve in 1955: how to build a three-bedroom home on a steep lot in Los Angeles’s Silver Lake neighborhood and give the people inside a sweeping view without putting their whole lives on display. Lautner designed the 1,679-square-foot home for Rosemary and Joseph Baldwin.

items.title: South African Airways Pilot Salary in 2026
items.summary: South African Airways is the national flag carrier of South Africa and one of the country’s most established airlines. Headquartered in Johannesburg, the airline operates domestic, regional and international services connecting South Africa with destinations across Africa and other international markets. Following its restructuring and relaunch in 2021, South African Airways has gradually rebuilt its operations, expanded its network and strengthened its position in the African aviation industry.

items.title: Keanu Reeves' 121-Minute Dark Fantasy Is As Close to Perfect As Superhero Movies Get
items.summary: The definition of a cult superhero film, Francis Lawrence and Keanu Reeves ' 2005 DC adaptation, Constantine, has developed a second life among devotees of its star and '90s-gothic style — and an upcoming sequel is among the most anticipated in recent superhero memory. Constantine did well at the box office, but seemed to drop off the cultural map after leaving theaters, despite its status as probably the single most visually striking comic book film ever made.

items.title: A Classic Twilight Zone Episode Is Like A Sci-Fi Version Of An Agatha Christie Mystery
items.summary: The second season of "The Twilight Zone" has some of the series' greatest twist endings, as the show proved unafraid to push into even more out-there science fiction and fantasy. One absolutely outrageous ending I haven't forgotten since childhood comes at the end of "The Twilight Zone" Season 2 Episode 28, "Will The Real Martian Please Stand Up?", written by series creator Rod Serling. Somewhere in the rural United States, on a dark winter night, a UFO crashes out of the sky. Two state troopers investigate and track the missing pilot to a roadside diner, where a bus trip to Boston has stopped over for food and rest.

items.title: The Aircraft Set To Replace British Airways’ Boeing 777-200ERs At London Heathrow
items.summary: British Airways (BA) is about to retire the aircraft that built its long-haul network, but it has not told anyone exactly what will take its place at London Heathrow (LHR). The airline ’s 43 Boeing 777-200ER s average roughly 26 years of age, according to Aerospace Global News, and most of them fly from Heathrow rather than Gatwick. The one firm date BA has given belongs to the other London airport: in a February 27, 2026 message to colleagues, CEO Sean Doyle said the first new Boeing 787-10 will be delivered to Gatwick in 2029, as published by the British Airways Media Centre.

items.title: Retired Navy A-6 Intruder Transported by CH-53K to MCB Quantico
items.summary: The A-6 Intruder was transported as an external load by a CH-53K from Naval Support Facility Dahlgren, Virginia, to Marine Corps Air Facility Quantico, a few dozen miles away. items.summary: ATLANTA – Delta Air Lines (DL) restored its aircraft weight-and-balance automation system on November 22 after a technical failure disrupted flights across the United States, forcing crews to rely on manual calculations and creating widespread delays ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush. items.title: Bears don’t sleep all winter, and other cold-weather animal myths
items.summary: It’s almost winter in the Northern Hemisphere. While the humans fire up their furnaces (or, ideally, heat pumps ), animals prepare in their own ways. That brings to mind a number of misconceptions people have about animals in the winter. Most of us were taught things that, over time, were proven to be untrue, and winter behaviors are no exception. Bears, for example, don’t sleep the entire winter. Birds don’t actually care about the cold that much, and migrate for other reasons. And squirrels aren’t constantly forgetting the location of their nuts.

items.title: The Crucified Tongkonan of Tolu Deri in North Toraja Regency, Indonesia

items.title: I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days

items.title: JetBrains Air in GoLand: Build, Review, and Profile Go Code With Agents
items.summary: If you’ve ever built backend services in Go, chances are you’ve also written a webhook handler or two. They’re small and rarely get much attention – that is, until something breaks. A third-party provider sends a signed request, and then you check the signature, store the event, and reply. Sounds like three easy steps, but a lot can go wrong. A captured request could get replayed, a duplicate could get saved twice, or a forged signature could slip through. Coding agents are not likely to make these types of mistakes, so with code becoming cheaper to generate, handlers are a good task to give them.
